sensors: Logger power input
about: Voltage of the battery that runs the logger. The logger works from 9.6 to 16 V.
reasonable: 12 to 14 V on a healthy solar-charged battery, with a daily cycle of a few tenths of a volt. Lowest just before sunrise in winter.
watch_for: A slow decline over days means the panel or battery is failing. Below about 11 V measurements become unreliable and below 9.6 V the logger stops, which is when clocks reset and records go missing.

sensors: Thermistor on the logger wiring panel
about: Temperature of the logger itself, used as the reference for thermocouples.
reasonable: Follows air temperature but lags it and runs warmer in sun inside the enclosure.
watch_for: Not an air temperature. Useful as a cross-check: if it disagrees wildly with air temperature one of them is wrong.

about: Temperature of the air, measured inside a radiation shield.
reasonable: Northern continental sites run from about -45 in winter to 30 or more in summer. Day to night swings of 10 to 15 degrees are normal; changes of more than a few degrees between 30-minute records are not.
watch_for: Values pinned at exactly -40 or 60 are the end of the sensor output range, not real readings. A flat line means a failed probe or a wiring fault.

about: Water vapour in the air as a percentage of saturation.
reasonable: Usually 20 to 100%. Near 100% at night, in fog and over snow; lowest on warm afternoons.
watch_for: Readings a little above 100 (to about 103) happen near saturation and are normally capped at 100 rather than removed. Values stuck at 0 or far above 100 mean a failed sensor. Accuracy drifts upward with age.

sensors: 05103 Wind Monitor (+/-3 degrees, 355 degree electrical range)
about: Direction the wind is coming from, clockwise from north.
reasonable: Any value from 0 to 360. Meaningless when wind speed is near zero.
watch_for: The potentiometer has a 5 degree gap near north. Do not average directions as ordinary numbers; the app averages them as directions.

sensors: 05103 Wind Monitor (0 to 100 m/s, +/-0.3 m/s or 1%, starts turning at 1.0 m/s); WindSonic
about: Horizontal wind speed.
reasonable: Mostly 0 to 10 m/s at a sheltered site, gusts to 20 or 30 in storms.
watch_for: Long runs of exactly 0 in winter usually mean the propeller is iced or snow-loaded, not calm air. Speeds below the 1 m/s starting threshold read as 0.

sensors: Calculated: incoming minus reflected shortwave
about: Sunlight absorbed by the surface.
reasonable: Zero at night, up to about 800 at midday over dark vegetation, much less over snow.
watch_for: Negative daytime values mean the reflected reading is larger than the incoming one: a covered upper dome or swapped channels.

sensors: Calculated: incoming minus outgoing longwave
about: Longwave gained from the sky minus longwave lost by the surface.
reasonable: About -100 under clear sky to near 0 under low cloud or fog. The CNR4 manual gives -100 as typical.
watch_for: Large positive values are not physical and point to a body temperature fault.

sensors: CM3 and the pyranometers in the CNR1 / CNR4 (305 to 2800 nm; daily totals within +/-10%)
about: Sunlight reaching the up-facing pyranometer.
reasonable: Zero at night. Up to about 500 under cloud and up to 1000 to 1300 at noon under clear summer sky (CNR1 manual, table A-1).
watch_for: Night values of a few W/m2 below zero are a normal thermal offset. Sustained daytime zeros in summer mean snow, frost or dirt on the dome. Values above about 1400 are not physical.

sensors: Down-facing pyranometer of the CNR1 / CNR4
about: Sunlight reflected by the ground or snow.
reasonable: 0 to about 150 over vegetation and up to 400 on clear days (CNR1 manual); much higher over snow, where most of the incoming light is reflected.
watch_for: Should never exceed incoming shortwave for long. If it does the upper dome is covered or the two channels are swapped.

sensors: Calculated: reflected / incoming shortwave
about: Share of sunlight that the surface reflects.
reasonable: About 0.1 to 0.2 over forest and wet peat, 0.2 to 0.3 over dry vegetation, 0.7 to 0.9 over fresh snow.
watch_for: Only meaningful in daylight. At night and at low sun it divides by nearly zero and gives huge or negative numbers, so use midday values or daily totals.

sensors: Pyrgeometers (CG3) in the CNR1 / CNR4
about: The net longwave exchange between the sensor and what it faces, before the sensor body temperature is added back.
reasonable: Up-facing: about -100 under clear sky to about 0 under low cloud. Down-facing: close to 0.
watch_for: This is not the true longwave flux. Use the corrected columns (lw_in, lw_out) for energy balance work.

sensors: Pyrgeometers in the CNR1 / CNR4 with the Pt-100 or thermistor body temperature
about: Thermal infrared radiation from the sky (in) and from the surface (out).
reasonable: Incoming: about 150 in clear arctic winter to 400 or more under warm cloud. Outgoing: about 200 at -30 C to 450 or more at +25 C.
watch_for: Outgoing longwave follows surface temperature closely; if it does not, the body temperature reading is wrong. A missing temperature reading makes both corrected columns missing.

sensors: CNR1 / CNR4 (sum of four components); NR-Lite
about: All incoming minus all outgoing radiation.
reasonable: About -100 on clear nights to 600 to 800 at midday in summer. Slightly negative through most of the winter.
watch_for: Spikes of thousands of W/m2 come from one bad component, usually the body temperature.

sensors: HFT3 (+/-100 W/m2, better than 5%); HFP01 (+/-2000 W/m2)
about: Heat flowing into (positive) or out of the ground at the plate depth.
reasonable: A few tens of W/m2 either way; larger in thawing peat in early summer.
watch_for: Readings at the +/-100 limit of the HFT3 are clipped.

sensors: SR50A, SnowVUE10
about: How clean the echo was for each snow depth reading.
reasonable: 152 to 210 is a good reading. 210 to 300 is reduced strength. 0 means no echo.
watch_for: Above 300 the distance is uncertain; snowfall, blowing snow and a tilted or frosted sensor all raise it. Screen snow depth with this column.

sensors: SR50A (0.5 to 10 m, +/-1 cm or 0.4% of distance); SnowVUE10 (0.2%)
about: An ultrasonic sensor measures the distance down to the snow or ground. Depth is the bare-ground distance minus that.
reasonable: Depth from 0 to about 1 to 1.5 m at boreal sites. Distance columns sit near the mounting height (1 to 3 m).
watch_for: The speed of sound depends on air temperature, so an uncorrected reading drifts with the daily temperature cycle. Small negative depths in summer are vegetation growth or a slightly wrong bare-ground distance.

sensors: TE525 (1 tip resolution, +/-1% up to 50 mm/h, works from 0 to 50 C)
about: Rain collected in each recording interval.
reasonable: Zero most of the time. A few mm per half hour in ordinary rain, 10 to 30 in a thunderstorm.
watch_for: An unheated tipping bucket does not measure snow; winter totals are melt, not snowfall. Long dry spells in a wet season often mean a blocked funnel.

sensors: Geonor T-200B (600 mm capacity, 0.05 mm sensitivity, 0.1% of full scale); OTT Pluvio
about: A weighing gauge reports the accumulated total in the bucket, rain and snow together.
reasonable: Rises in steps during precipitation and is flat otherwise. Drops only when the bucket is emptied.
watch_for: Wind and temperature make the total wobble by a few tenths of a mm. A sudden fall is servicing, not negative precipitation. Take differences to get amounts per interval.

about: The raw signal from a water content reflectometer, before conversion to water content.
reasonable: About 14 with the rods in air and about 42 in saturated soil.
watch_for: Frozen soil reads like dry soil because ice does not respond like liquid water.

sensors: CS616 (+/-2.5% with standard calibration); CS650 / CS655 (+/-3% typical); Stevens Hydra Probe
about: Volume of liquid water per volume of soil.
reasonable: 0.05 to 0.5 in mineral soil; 0.2 to 0.9 in peat. Drops sharply when the soil freezes and recovers at thaw.
watch_for: Factory calibrations are for mineral soil and read wrong in peat without a soil-specific calibration. 7999 or NAN means the probe did not answer.

sensors: CS650 / CS655 (+/-5% of reading + 0.05 dS/m); Hydra Probe
about: How well the wet soil conducts electricity, a measure of dissolved salts.
reasonable: Close to 0 in peat and rain-fed soils, up to 1 to 2 in mineral soils.
watch_for: Falls to zero when the soil freezes.

sensors: 107 thermistor (-35 to 50 C); 109 thermistor (-50 to 70 C); both about +/-0.1 to 0.2 C; CS650 (+/-0.1 to 0.5 C)
about: Temperature of the soil, peat or snow at a fixed depth.
reasonable: Deep probes change slowly and stay near 0 C for weeks during freeze and thaw. Near-surface probes range from about -20 to 25.
watch_for: A probe that tracks air temperature has been exposed by frost heave or thaw. Sudden jumps of tens of degrees, or values like -80, are broken leads or a failed channel.

about: Air pressure at the station.
reasonable: Within about 30 hPa of the site average; roughly 1013 at sea level and about 12 hPa less per 100 m of elevation.
watch_for: Steps of several hPa between records are not weather.
